newsitem.title: UK: Reuters says sterling strength hits revenue.
newsitem.headline: Reuters says sterling strength hits revenue.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Wednesday that the strong pound resulted in a two percent fall in first quarter revenue to 699 million pounds, or $1,139 million.

Chief executive Peter Job said in a statement that if the pound remained at current levels, the company expected to announce little or no growth in reported pre-tax profit and earnings at the half-year stage.
Reuters said underlying growth in first quarter revenue was eight percent from a year earlier.
"Sterling's strength continues to have a negative impact on our reported figures," Job said.

"Meantime, the business is performing much as we expected. We mainly invoice in local currency all over the world so sterling exchange rate movements are not having any impact on unit sales," he said.

He said the company was making steady progress towards its year end target for its new 3000 range of financial information products and said newer business lines including risk management software and business information sales to corporations were also performing steadily.
"Instinet, our electronic equities trading subsidiary, continues to do well and foreign exchange transaction revenue at comparable rates is up on last year," Job added.
Sterling currency conversions are at a rate of $1.63, a rate prevailing at March 31.
